name: Tech House
about: Tech house is the meeting point of house's swing and techno's minimal tool-making: four-to-the-floor at around 125 beats per minute, tight percussion, dubby chords and a bassline doing most of the talking. The name came out of London in the mid-1990s, around Mr. C's club The End, Eddie Richards' Wiggle parties and Terry Francis, with a parallel German strain on Poker Flat and Moon Harbour. In the late 2000s Loco Dice, Jamie Jones's Hot Creations and Claude VonStroke's Dirtybird made it the sound of Ibiza terraces, and by the mid-2010s it was the biggest dance genre in Europe, led by Solardo, Fisher and Patrick Topping. Purists hear the early, dubby version; the charts hear the loud one.

artists.name: Mr. C
artists.why: The End's founder, popularised the term

artists.name: Layo & Bushwacka!
artists.why: The End's residents turned album act

artists.name: Steve Bug
artists.why: Poker Flat and the German strain

artists.name: Hot Since 82
artists.why: Knee Deep in Sound's chart-friendly groove

albums.title: Tourism
albums.why: New York's tribal answer to the London sound, long, hypnotic and percussive, and the album that showed tech house could carry a whole record.

albums.title: Around the House
albums.why: Matthew Herbert sampled his kitchen and Dani Siciliano's voice into the most intimate house album of the decade, tech house at its most musical.

albums.title: Architecture
albums.why: The Wiggle founder's album is the sound of The End's early years on record: dubby, swung, patient, and built for a dark room.

albums.title: Profound Sounds Vol. 1
albums.why: Wink's Ovum mix caught the moment house and techno DJs started playing the same records, and it still sounds like a working set.

albums.title: Volksworld
albums.why: The German wing's founding album, clean and funky, with the reduced drum programming Poker Flat would make its house style.

albums.title: Low Life
albums.why: The End's residents made the first great tech house album, cinematic, breakbeat-tinged and anchored by the club's dubby low end.

albums.title: Fabric 01
albums.why: The mix that opened the Fabric series and defined its house: Richards' wonky, dubby, London-after-hours selection remains a touchstone.

albums.title: Loud
albums.why: Maas took the tribal tech-house groove to the album charts with big-room drops and guest vocals; dated in places, undeniable at its peaks.

albums.title: Night Works
albums.why: Love Story made them a name, but the album around it is their The End residency rendered as a late-night film score.

albums.title: Beware of the Bird
albums.why: Dirtybird's founder brought Detroit bass and a sense of humour to tech house, with Who's Afraid of Detroit? as the calling card.

albums.title: From a Deep Place
albums.why: Voorn's debut album sits between Detroit techno and the Dutch tech house of his sets, melodic, warm and precisely mixed.

albums.title: Late Bloomers
albums.why: Cocoon released Gerber's debut as a melancholy, melodic tech house album, and it set the tone for the Ibiza terrace sound that followed.

albums.title: 7 Dunham Place
albums.why: The Desolat founder's first album turned his percussive, dubbed-out DJ sound into a coherent set, the late-2000s tech house template.

albums.title: Restless
albums.why: The Moon Harbour boss's debut is German tech house at its most elegant, reduced grooves with a jazz player's touch.

albums.title: Don't You Remember the Future
albums.why: Jones's Crosstown Rebels debut mixed disco edits, dubby tech house and pop instincts, the blueprint for everything Hot Creations did next.

albums.title: Bird Brain
albums.why: The second Dirtybird album is looser and goofier than the first, but Vocal Chords and Big Pants earned their long club lives.

albums.title: Crash Test
albums.why: The engineer behind Loco Dice and Timo Maas steps forward with a precise, dubby set that treats tech house as studio craft.

albums.title: Efunk: The Album
albums.why: Boston's Soul Clap pushed Hot Creations-era tech house toward R&B and boogie, with real singers and a sense of play.

albums.title: Ghettos & Gardens
albums.why: Dirtybird's second major album is a West Coast party record, bass-heavy tech house with a melodic streak and Don't Go as the hit.

albums.title: Different Sides of the Sun
albums.why: Jamie Jones and Lee Foss's supergroup made the Hot Creations sound a pop proposition, with Benediction and Reverse Skydiving leading.

albums.title: Comfort
albums.why: Coles sings and produces across a moody, deep-leaning debut that shows how far tech house had drifted toward bedroom pop by 2013.

albums.title: 8-track
albums.why: The Knee Deep in Sound boss's first album is streamlined festival tech house with the melodic sense that separates him from the pack.

albums.title: Nobody Is Not Loved
albums.why: The Diynamic founder's second album is a guest-heavy, melodic house record; more terrace soundtrack than statement, but fluently made.

albums.title: Recovery
albums.why: A lockdown album written about addiction and rehab, Recovery is more personal than the first and less consistent on the dancefloor.
